title: Shadow onboarding: 12-day technical deploy kickoff
content:
Purpose:
This working doc describes a compact 12-day shadow-first onboarding for senior technical hires who will join the Serving Runtime / Inference teams and need to be ramped into a technical deploy cadence quickly. Goals: reduce time-to-first-merge, minimize context-switch cost for manager and buddy, ensure hardware/networking is ready for remote hires, and capture interview-to-onboard signals for future hiring calibration.

Audience:
- People Ops (owners)
- Hiring manager (eng-serving-runtime)
- Buddy / mentor (assigned from team)
- New hire (candidate accepted)

Quick overview (one-liner):
A lightweight 12-day sequenced plan: 3-day preboarding + 7-day shadow + 2-day hands-on ramp to first small deploy task. Includes interview-rubric review, hardware checklist for remote GPU access, and asynchronous evidence capture.

Pre-boarding (day -3 to -1):
- Day -3: HR welcome email with schedule, manager intro, buddy intro. Attachments: access matrix, SSO steps, VPN + MFA instructions.
- Day -2: Tech ops ticket raised (see linked_artifacts) for remote hardware provisioning; confirm GPU node access (reserved test slot), SSH key upload, and KMS access for sandbox.
- Day -1: Team async orientation notes (video snippets): architecture intro, serving runtime flow diagram (5min), common debug commands. New hire asked to complete: SSO login, set up local dev env, and join #team-runtime.

Day 0 — Quiet launch (first day):
- Morning: manager welcome (30m) — expectation setting, top 3 priorities.
- Midday: buddy runbook walkthrough (45m) — team rituals, deploy checklist, how we open incidents.
- Afternoon: micro-assignment: read/annotate one lightweight PR (non-blocking), leave one comment.
- Notes to self: keep day 0 lightweight. Avoid heavy architecture deep dives.

Days 1–7 — Shadow sprint (observe + annotate):
- Each day buddy schedules 2x 1-hour windows where new hire shadows:
  - 1st window: morning standup + task triage (observe how routes are prioritized)
  - 2nd window: deploy walkthrough + postmortem review (if any)
- New hire tasks during shadow week:
  - maintain a 1-line daily learning log in the shared doc
  - run a non-prod deploy simulation with buddy (no write perms to prod) by day 5
  - identify one small cleanup / doc fix to own by day 7

Days 8–9 — Paired hands-on (apply with supervision):
- Day 8: New hire owns a test deploy (under mentor supervision). Checklist: preflight, smoke tests, rollback plan.
- Day 9: Post-deploy retrospective and minor followup (assignments to fix flaky test or instrumentation gap).

Day 10–11 — Independent small deliverable:
- Day 10: New hire implements the small cleanup/doc fix (PR created).
- Day 11: PR review, merge, end-to-end verification.

Day 12 — Handoff and signal capture:
- Final sync (manager + buddy + hire) 45m: review outcomes, remaining blockers, training needs.
- Capture ramp signals: code review quality, deploy shyness, infra access friction, docs ownership potential.
- Create follow-up plan for 30/60/90 based on observed strengths/deficits.

Interview rubric alignment (how we reuse interview evidence during onboarding):
- Before offer acceptance: hiring panel compiled strengths/concerns (scorecard IDs). This doc requires the hiring manager to paste the scorecard summary into the new hire folder before day 0.
- Use observed signals during shadow to validate or contradict interview concerns. Example rubric items and what to watch for in shadow:
  - System design: listens and asks clarifying Qs during deploy walkthough (signal = asked >2 clarifying Qs).
  - Debugging under pressure: ability to follow runbook and ask appropriate escalation Qs during simulated rollbacks.
  - Cross-team communication: how quickly they find relevant Slack threads / docs.
  - Ownership: volunteers for a doc fix or test to close a small gap.

Scoring template for shadow signals (quick, for manager use):
- 0: not observed / not applicable
- 1: observed, needs coaching
- 2: observed, meets expectation
- 3: observed, exceeds expectation
Fields to record: date, assessor name, rubric item id, score, short evidence note, recommended follow-up owner.

Remote hardware & network checklist (ops-actionable items):
- Confirmed test GPU slot (type: A10/A30/V100) — ticket number.
- SSH key added to infra: yes/no.
- VPN access validated and MFA set up.
- KMS test encrypt/decrypt completed.
- Container runtime versions documented (nvidia driver + cuda).
- Access to internal artifact registry (docker.pkg) granted.
- Reserved time in shared GPU pool for first deploy (2hrs window).
- Hardware fallback plan: have cloud-based ephemeral node available if local reserved node fails.

Hiring-plan appendix (snippet for cross-functional recruiters):
- Role summary: Senior Inference Engineer — short list criteria: 5+ years backend infra, 2+ projects shipping with GPU inference, track record of oncall or production deploys.
- Interview flow (recommended): phone screen (30m) -> take-home diagnostic (4hrs) -> onsite loop (4x interviews: infra, system-design, debugging-live, culture).
- Rubric anchors: each loop interviewer uses 1–4 scale for core competencies + explicit red flags. Red flags: inability to explain a past production incident, no experience with observability tooling.
- Offer cadence: target 7–10 days from final onsite to offer.

Unresolved questions / open decisions (notes for People Ops):
- Should we standardize the GPU model we reserve for all remote hires? (Pros: repeatable; Cons: cost)
- How to capture failed deploy behavior as a learning artifact (video of walkthrough?)
- Should the 12-day plan be extended to 16 for hires without prior cloud infra experience?

Links and artifacts to copy into new hire folder:
- onboarding checklist template: CONFLUENCE-12345
- recruit scorecard export: JIRA-HIRE-8721
- infra provisioning runbook: /docs/infra/provisioning.md
- buddy playbook: /playbooks/buddy-runbook.md

Quick templates (copy into new hire folder):
- Day 0 agenda (bullet list)
- Shadow evidence capture table (date | item | score | note | owner)
- Hardware ticket template: summary, required GPU, time window, contact ops owner

Notes to self (informal):
- keep this doc short; move larger policy bits to Confluence.
- ask Lena to run a pilot with 2 hires next quarter and measure time-to-first-merge.
- consider adding a simple automated survey at day 13 for new hire feedback (1–5 scale + 3 short answers).

Version history / edits log (informal):
- 2025-09-10 Priya: initial draft

- 2025-11-02 Lena: tweaked days 8–11 to reduce friction on manager time

End of doc.
